description: Writes the opening line of a letter or email for a name, in the language of the letter: "Sehr geehrte Frau Müller," in German, "Sayın Ahmet Bey," in Turkish, "Madame," in French. Returns formal, informal and neutral versions. When the gender is not certain enough, the gendered form is NOT guessed: `form` is "neutral" and `reason` says why. Use the returned line as it is; word order, punctuation and which name part is used differ by language. Pass `names` instead of `name` for up to 100 at once.

country.description: Country as an ISO code (TR, DE, US or TUR, DEU, USA) or a country name (Germany, Deutschland). When given, the answer is weighted by that country's data — the same name can have a different gender by country.

email.description: Email address, when no name is known: anna.mueller@ gives Frau Mueller.

gender.description: Known gender, e.g. from a CRM field. Skips the lookup.

ip.description: IP address of the person (IPv4 or IPv6), used to look up the country when neither `country` nor a locale with a region is given. It is not stored.

language.description: Language of the letter, not of the name: en, en-US, en-GB, de, de-AT, de-CH, fr, es, it, pt, pt-PT, pt-BR, nl, tr, pl, ja. Without it the locale's language is used, then the country's, then English.

locale.description: Language tag of the person, such as a browser's Accept-Language (it-IT, de-AT). Its region is used as the country when `country` is not given; a tag without a region (en) sets none.

min_probability.description: Below this gender probability the neutral form is used. Default 90.

name.description: Full name, e.g. "Anna Müller". Use `email` instead when there is no name.

names.description: Up to 100 full names (or email addresses with type "email"), answered in order.

type.description: With `names`: what the values are. Default: name.

name: salutation
title: Salutation for a letter or email
